title: They didn’t bow to statues anymore.
paragraphs: They didn’t bow to statues anymore.
No golden calves. No carved images. No incense burning in hidden rooms.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The lights dim. The crowd leans in. A name is announced—and the room erupts before a single word about Jesus is spoken.
That subtle shift where the message becomes secondary… and the messenger becomes everything.
But deep down, something feels off.
Because the applause lasts longer than the altar call.
Scripture doesn’t stutter when it comes to this.
“Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” — 1 John 5:21
Anything that takes the place of God in your heart.
Anything you rely on, exalt, or center your life around more than Him.
The modern church doesn’t struggle with lack of voices.
It struggles with who it worships.
You can quote sermons word for word.
You defend them online like family.
But when was the last time you trembled at the Word of God itself?
When was the last time you opened Scripture… not to prepare a post, not to share a clip… but to be confronted?
But when influence becomes identity… it becomes an idol.
When being seen matters more than being holy.
You follow more than you pray.
You scroll more than you seek.
You feel closer to a personality than to the presence of God.
And slowly, quietly… your heart shifts.
“Woe to you… for you love the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.” — Luke 11:43
This was spoken to religious leaders.
Here’s the breaking point most people avoid:
You can build a massive platform… and still be unknown to God.
“Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord…’ and then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you.’” — Matthew 7:22-23
That’s the difference between influence… and intimacy.
Because the Gospel doesn’t just expose idols.
You don’t need to earn your way back.
You don’t need to rebuild your image.
To lay down every name, every platform, every obsession… and come back to the feet of Jesus.
“Whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for My sake will find it.” — Matthew 16:25
Because letting go of influence feels like losing everything.
But what if what you’re holding… is what’s killing you?
What if the very thing you’ve built… is the thing keeping you from truly knowing Him?
There are two paths in front of you.
One leads to recognition, applause, and a name people remember.
The other leads to a cross… a narrow road… and a Savior who actually knows you.
And you already feel which one you’re on.
